notes:
Account summary:
- Aurora CX builds customer support automation (agent assist + auto-drafts + post-call/ticket summarization). They want to standardize LLM inference behind a single API with predictable latency/cost and better ops tooling than they have today.

Use case details (from discovery + POC scoping):
- Primary workflows:
  - Agent assist (chat-style, streaming required): suggest responses with citations from KB + recent ticket context.
  - Auto-draft / summarization: summarize long conversations + generate next-step actions and CRM fields.
  - Ticket triage: classify, route to queues, detect priority/escalation.
  - Optional: embeddings for KB retrieval + reranking.
- Volume / performance (directional, not final):
  - Peak hours: high concurrency during business hours; wants predictable p95 latency.
  - Target p95 for agent assist: "sub-second first token" and stable streaming (they called out disconnects as a hard fail).
  - Wants knobs for cost control (batching/caching), but not at the expense of interactive latency.

Key technical requirements (dependencies called out explicitly by their platform lead):
- Auth/SSO:
  - SSO/SAML required for Console access (their security team will not approve local-only accounts for admins).
  - RBAC: separate roles for app engineers vs security reviewers vs finance/procurement.
- Logging/audit:
  - Audit logs needed for admin actions and key events (API key creation/rotation, route changes, model pin changes, retention setting changes).
  - Retention controls: want an explicit statement of default log retention + ability to reduce retention; asked if we support export to their SIEM.
  - KMS: asked whether keys can be customer-managed for any stored artifacts (even if they opt for Hosted first).
- Routing / reliability:
  - Requires a clear fallback story: if a pinned model/region is degraded, route to compatible variant/region with guardrails.
  - They want deterministic behavior: explicit policy of when we fail over vs fail fast; they requested we show it in a live demo scenario ("graceful degradation without breaking app contracts").
  - Concerns about model rollouts: wants the ability to pin model versions and control rollouts during their peak support periods.
- Deployment:
  - Prefers VPC/private networking for production due to support transcript sensitivity; willing to start with Hosted for POC if security review is satisfied and data is synthetic.

Buying posture / stakeholders:
- Champion: ML Platform Lead (owner of inference layer) + Director of Support Ops (business owner).
- Security reviewer involved early; procurement will engage after security sign-off + preliminary POC results.
- Quote from scoping call: "We don’t want to be in the business of chasing model changes or GPU capacity; we just need it to be predictable."

POC framing (current draft):
- Objective: Replace their current patchwork (mixed providers + self-hosted experiments) with Redwood as primary inference runtime for agent assist + summarization.
- Success metrics (draft):
  - Latency: stable p95 and no streaming disconnects.
  - Cost: demonstrate measurable unit-cost reduction using caching/batching recommendations + token-level breakdown.
  - Reliability: demonstrate fallback routing and safe rollouts.
  - Security: SSO enabled for admins; audit logs + retention controls documented and reviewable.
- Data constraint: must use synthetic data in demo; POC may use anonymized/redacted transcripts only after security approval.

Demo tie-ins (what resonated / what to emphasize next time):
- Strongest: token-level cost/latency breakdown in Console; "production economics" story landed.
- Also strong: tool calling + structured output for ticket triage and form-fill (they liked that it reduces brittle parsing).
- Needs reinforcement: Dedicated vs Hosted explanation (they asked about noisy-neighbor and quota predictability).

Open questions / to confirm:
- Final throughput numbers for peak concurrency and expected context sizes.
- Whether they need data residency guarantees immediately (they hinted at a future EU expansion).
- Which model families are acceptable (they are open to curated open models but want a quality regression plan).

Internal notes:
- Keep Aurora POC tenant separate from sales demo tenant (they asked for access to live dashboards; do not reuse demo org).
- Next meeting should include routing/fallback owner + security SME to answer audit/retention questions cleanly (avoid hand-wavy responses).
